stories.new_fact: AP reported November 6 that election outcomes put data-center siting, electricity prices, water, and affordability under heightened political scrutiny in major data-center states including Ohio.
stories.new_takeaway: For a financed data-center project, local consent, utility terms, and permits are underwriting inputs rather than peripheral political risk.
stories.why_now: This is new post-election reporting on the development constraint after the November 5 episode covered local zoning testimony.
stories.previous_coverage: The prior seven episodes did not cover the national election-driven data-center siting constraint or its infrastructure-finance implication.
stories.uncertainty: No new federal rule or universal project restriction has been enacted; individual approvals and state policies control.
stories.watch: Filed state bills, utility tariffs, permit conditions, and specific local actions.

stories.new_fact: Axios reported five Central Ohio communities voted on data-center issues, including Grove City’s referendum requirement and restrictions approved in Granville, Pataskala, and Sunbury.
stories.new_takeaway: The practical local question is the adopted municipality-specific rule, project size, water demand, and process—not a broad conclusion about all computing facilities.
stories.why_now: The results were reported after the prior episode and create concrete local procedural changes.
stories.previous_coverage: November 4 covered Columbus Council Issues 8 and 9; these are distinct data-center ballot results in several Central Ohio communities.
stories.uncertainty: Certification, ordinance text, enforcement, litigation, and project-specific effects remain unresolved.
stories.watch: Certified results, ballot language, municipal implementation, revised project plans, and litigation.

stories.new_fact: Freddie Mac Bulletin 2026-15 immediately reclassifies co-owner buyout refinance mortgages from cash-out to no-cash-out and broadens them to the no-cash-out eligibility framework, subject to requirements.
stories.new_takeaway: Lenders must reset product selection, file documentation, underwriting, pricing, and delivery checks for equity-buyout files; the guide change is not a universal approval claim.
stories.why_now: The November 4 bulletin is a fresh, immediate operational change not used in the November 5 edition.
stories.previous_coverage: Recent lending segments used manual underwriting, lender economics, scoring, and servicing; this is a distinct borrower-product and refinance-classification change.
stories.uncertainty: Lender overlays, borrower credit and income, collateral, ownership documentation, and exact guide provisions still determine each loan.
stories.watch: Lender implementation notices, pricing overlays, delivery guidance, and borrower-file outcomes.

stories.new_fact: A pre-registered paper tested four open-weight models in five harnesses across 156 simulated retail-bank cases and found meaningful model-harness performance differences, including a 11.5-point within-model spread for one model.
stories.new_takeaway: A bank should validate a model together with its search, memory, tool, reviewer, and action-log design rather than accept a model-level score.
stories.why_now: The paper was posted November 4 and supplies fresh measured evidence after recent bank-AI segments focused on bank and vendor disclosures.
stories.previous_coverage: The prior seven episodes did not cover this experiment’s action-trace finding or model-harness comparison.
stories.uncertainty: It is a simulated retail bank using open-weight models, not a production deployment or independent real-bank outcome.
stories.watch: Independent replication, named-bank controlled trials, real exception evidence, and action-log validation results.
stories.ledger_row_changed: Simulated retail-bank agent experiment, lane 8 compliance/model risk: new research-paper row with action-trace measurement and no production metric.

stories.new_fact: OpenAI released GPT-6 Cyber to selected approved Daybreak Red customers and reported 48.5% on ExploitGym versus 32.1% for GPT-5.6 Cyber plus scope-adherence results.
stories.new_takeaway: A cyber agent’s authorization boundary is an operational capability constraint, so a model benchmark must be evaluated alongside scope controls and human verification.
stories.why_now: OpenAI announced this model version and evaluation on November 5.
stories.previous_coverage: November 5 covered Daybreak Red’s GovCloud route for GPT-5.6 Cyber; this is a different model, benchmark comparison, access cohort, and security capability change.
stories.uncertainty: OpenAI is the evaluator; restricted access and controlled benchmarks do not prove bank-network outcomes, remediation quality, or misuse rates.
stories.watch: Independent replication, false-positive and patch-quality evidence, access expansion, and safeguard results.

stories.new_fact: Freddie Mac’s November 5 survey gives current weekly rate context, and NWS hourly forecasts guide Columbus travel timing.
stories.new_takeaway: A survey average and an overnight forecast are decision context, not individual loan or route outcomes.
stories.previous_coverage: No prior numerical forecast is repeated.
stories.uncertainty: Individual rates and weather conditions vary and update.
stories.watch: Live loan estimates and NWS hourly conditions.

ai_banking_card.institution_and_task: Pre-registered simulated retail-bank agent experiment; action selection under consumer-credit, payments, investment, privacy, and AML conduct rules
ai_banking_card.lane: 8 - compliance, model risk, audit, and QC
ai_banking_card.ledger_row_changed: New research-paper row for the model-harness pair and action-log evaluation
ai_banking_card.disclosed_metric_and_baseline: 87.3% to 92.1% pooled correct-case range; 11.5-point within-model harness spread; no production baseline
ai_banking_card.large_bank_change: Validate the exact model-harness pair and executed action logs, not only a model’s conversational output.
ai_banking_card.limitation: Simulated cases, open-weight models, and no production customer or loss evidence.
ai_banking_card.next_dated_event: No date announced; revisit on replication or a named bank controlled trial.

frontier_ai_card.item_and_primary_source: OpenAI GPT-6 Cyber, November 5 primary announcement
frontier_ai_card.what_is_new: GPT-6 Cyber is initially available to selected approved Daybreak Red customers and OpenAI reports version-specific exploit and scope results.
frontier_ai_card.new_capability: The model is reported to find and validate exploits more successfully while adhering more reliably to task scope.
frontier_ai_card.measurement: OpenAI reports ExploitGym 48.5% versus GPT-5.6 Cyber’s 32.1% and scope-test results; these are provider evaluations.
frontier_ai_card.tradeoff_or_limit: Restricted access, controlled benchmarks, and authorization failure risk mean the results do not establish production security or remediation quality.
frontier_ai_card.who_and_condition: Approved defenders benefit only when targets, permissions, review, and escalation are properly bounded.
frontier_ai_card.bridge: A regulated bank could first use it in a sandboxed internal software-security assessment, gated by written authorization and human verification before remediation or any production action.

editorial_review.notes: Eight candidates were recorded before story-tracker.md was consulted. Four selected substantive stories are within 48 hours: the AP national data-center report, Central Ohio ballot reporting, Freddie Mac Bulletin 2026-15, the bank-agent harness paper, and GPT-6 Cyber. The local story is distinct from the previously covered Columbus charter measures. Lending uses a new borrower-product/refinance workflow. Banking AI explicitly labels research evidence, a simulation, and the absence of a production metric. Frontier AI distinguishes OpenAI’s measurements from independent validation. Script contains seven chapters, exactly three closing watch items, a 35-50 word payoff, and substantive cohost questions with answers.
